reasons: By-hour UTC is severely concentrated: hours 16 (+2992) and 17 (+3758) generate all the profit, while hours 14 (-2454) and 15 (-2503) are strongly negative. Removing hour 16 alone flips total P&L negative (-152); removing hour 17 alone flips it to -917. The result is essentially the intraday window of 16-17 UTC, not a broadly distributed edge.

No stated mechanism is given for why profit should persist in exactly these two hours while the strategy simultaneously trades two other hours that consistently lose money — this looks like an unfiltered time-of-day exposure rather than a deliberate regime.

61% of sessions lose money (235/384) and the top 5% of trades supply 39% of profit, consistent with a strategy reliant on a narrow set of large winners rather than broad-based edge; combined with the hourly concentration this further indicates fragility.

Monthly distribution is also narrow at the top: the three biggest months (2025-04 +1161, 2025-11 +897, 2024-08 +720) together contribute ~2778 of the ~2840 net, so removing them takes the result to roughly breakeven.
auditors.confidence_note: I cannot see any out-of-sample evidence, nor trade-level or session-level P&L series, nor a stated rationale for the intraday window; my judgement rests solely on the concentration signals visible in the by-hour, by-month, and outcome aggregates.
